newsitem.title: USA: Dole demands Clinton answer questions on donations.
newsitem.headline: Dole demands Clinton answer questions on donations.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole demanded Monday that President Clinton answer questions about his links to Asian businessmen and their contributions to Democratic Party coffers.

Speaking to reporters before boarding a plane in Kansas City, Dole echoed questions raised by other Republicans about the campaign contributions and their potential impact on Clinton's foreign policy. "Not some slip, slide and duck, Mr. President. Just answer the questions," Dole said.

House Speaker Newt Gingrich Sunday said investigations were "unavoidable" into contacts between Clinton and Asian businessmen, including an Indonesian couple's $425,000 contribution to the Democratic Party and another donation from a South Korean company that the party returned after media queries about it.

When Dole was first asked about the matter Monday by reporters in Kansas City, he indicated he might wait until Tuesday to comment. But just before boarding a plane to San Diego, he said his campaign had raised questions about the issue and thought Clinton should respond immediately.

"There are a whole lot of problems here that have been raised," Dole said. "Taking money from a foreign nation.They gave it back when somebody caught them, but why did they do it? Why did he (Clinton) meet with these people? Did it have any impact on the policies in East Timor (which was incorporated into Indonesia in 1976)?...We're going to raise the questions every day until the president's properly responded."

Clinton's ties to Indonesian billionaire James Riady have been fiercely attacked by Republicans, who say the wealthy Indonesian has exerted influence over the president by contributing to his political causes.
